root_cause.text: In the Bluetooth MGMT advertising TLV parser, `tlv_data_is_valid()` accessed the type byte `data[i + 1]` before verifying that the current TLV element length fit within the supplied buffer, allowing an out-of-bounds read on malformed input.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states "`tlv_data_is_valid()` reads each advertising data field length from `data[i]`, then inspects `data[i + 1]` ... before checking that the current field still fits inside the supplied buffer," and the patch fixes this by moving `if (i + cur_len >= len) return false;` before all `data[i + 1]` type checks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length bounds check in TLV validation to reject malformed fields that exceed the buffer size.
intent_record.what: A new bounds check was added in tlv_data_is_valid(): after skipping zero-length fields, the function now tests whether i + cur_len >= len and immediately returns false if the current TLV field would extend past the provided data length.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this rejects malformed TLV/EIR data whose declared field length would exceed the available buffer, preventing subsequent access to data[i + 1] and later parsing from operating on out-of-bounds input.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an overly strict TLV length validation in tlv_data_is_valid() so valid advertising data is not incorrectly rejected.
intent_record.what: The change removes a four-line validation block from tlv_data_is_valid() that checked whether the current TLV field length would exceed the total buffer length by testing `if (i + cur_len >= len) return false;`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer rejects advertising data solely because the current field span reaches or exceeds the total length at this point in the loop, allowing such TLV data to be treated as valid instead of returning false from this specific boundary check.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly adds the missing TLV length/bounds validation needed to prevent reading past the supplied buffer on malformed input, which matches the root cause of the out-of-bounds read in tlv_data_is_valid().

The root cause is an out-of-bounds read from accessing the TLV type byte before confirming the element fits in the buffer. This change instead relaxes a strict length validation to avoid rejecting valid data, which is a functional validation adjustment rather than a fix for the bounds-check ordering bug.

candidates.rationale: This statement dereferences data[i + 1] before validating that the current TLV element fits within the remaining buffer. On malformed input where the element length exceeds the supplied size, this read can go out of bounds.

Bluetooth: Fix advertising instance validity check for flags

Flags are not allowed in Scan Response.

Signed-off-by: Sz
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 9c9db78dc0fbbd95177fefdad008e46ffaa777f2
Author: Szymon Janc <szymon.janc@codecoup.pl>
Date:   Sun Sep 18 12:50:06 2016 +0200

    Bluetooth: Fix advertising instance validity check for flags
    
    Flags are not allowed in Scan Response.
    
    Signed-off-by: Szymon Janc <szymon.janc@codecoup.pl>
    Signed-off-by: Marcel Holtmann <marcel@holtmann.org>

diff --git a/net/bluetooth/mgmt.c b/net/bluetooth/mgmt.c
index c96b0adc4971..2758c6a4425c 100644
--- a/net/bluetooth/mgmt.c
+++ b/ne
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because the vulnerable access pattern is visible directly in the snippet. In `tlv_data_is_valid(...)`, inside the loop `for (i = 0, cur_len = 0; i < len; i += (cur_len + 1))`, the code sets `cur_len = data[i];` and then immediately reads `data[i + 1]` in `if (data[i + 1] == EIR_FLAGS && (!is_adv_data || flags_managed(adv_flags)))` and again in `if (data[i + 1] == EIR_TX_POWER && tx_power_managed(adv_flags))`. There is no prior bounds check ensuring that `i + 1 < len` or that the TLV element length fits within the supplied buffer before these reads. That matches the stated root cause: accessing the type byte before validating the current TLV element length, which can cause an out-of-bounds read on malformed input. The commit only changes the semantic condition for `EIR_FLAGS` (`(!is_adv_data || flags_managed(adv_flags))`) to forbid flags in scan response; it does not add any length/bounds validation before `data[i + 1]` is accessed. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix for the OOB-read issue is not yet included.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the full `tlv_data_is_valid()` loop and the ordering of checks. The vulnerable construct is present: inside the loop, after `cur_len = data[i];`, the code immediately reads `data[i + 1]` in multiple conditions such as `if (data[i + 1] == EIR_FLAGS && flags_managed(adv_flags))`, `if (data[i + 1] == EIR_TX_POWER && tx_power_managed(adv_flags))`, `if (data[i + 1] == EIR_NAME_COMPLETE && name_managed(adv_flags))`, `if (data[i + 1] == EIR_NAME_SHORT && name_managed(adv_flags))`, and `if (data[i + 1] == EIR_APPEARANCE && appearance_managed(adv_flags))`. These accesses occur before the later bounds check comment `/* If the current field length would exceed the total data ... */`, i.e. before verifying that the current TLV element actually fits within `len`. Therefore malformed input with an incomplete element can cause an out-of-bounds read of the type byte, matching the root cause. The fix is not present here because the code still dereferences `data[i + 1]` prior to validating the element length.
